title: pvOMETIFFChannelCalculator
body:
## pvOMETIFFChannelCalculator

Combines up to ten fluorescence-microscopy channels of an OME-TIFF image into one RGBA colour image. Each enabled point array named Channel_1 to Channel_10 (the names pvOMETIFFReader produces) is mapped through its ChannelNLUT lookup table, its opacity is multiplied by ChannelNWeight, and the channels are blended additively into a new unsigned-char point array named Colors; the input image and its arrays are passed through unchanged. Use it to make a false-colour composite for display or PNG export; the channel data themselves are not modified.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Every enabled channel needs a lookup table: an enabled array without a ChannelNLUT stops the filter with "No LUT specified". Connect a pvResourcePVLookupTable to the matching ChannelNLUT input (opacity mapping on) for each channel you enable.
- Lookup tables and weights are keyed by the names Channel_1 to Channel_10; arrays with other names cannot be given a lookup table.
- ParaView's GUI creates default colour maps (blue, green, red, magenta, cyan, grey) when the proxy is initialized with input data available; Schemaxis has not verified that this happens for its nodes, so connect the tables explicitly.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `OMETIFFChannelCalculator`. Identity: `filters/OMETIFFChannelCalculator`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.
